pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has the NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' CHECK. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks the labels on high and low items and none on normal ones. The code is in src/index.js `item`.
test 'AC-3' checks each of the three filters, with items in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks the unfiltered list in id order.
test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav HTML for all four views, with the current filter in <strong> and not a link.
test 'AC-6' checks a 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, an empty value and __proto__.
test 'AC-7' checks the exact messages for high, low and normal, and 'No items yet.' in all four views with an empty table.
traffic/routes.json contains /?priority=high. test 'AC-8' asserts it. The traffic config check now accepts queries.

findings.what: The last commit, 'Follow-up edits', loosened the 'No match' state test from toBe('No low-priority items.') to toBeDefined(). `message()` returns a string or null, never undefined, so the assertion can never fail. The commit message says nothing about this, and the PR says no tests were loosened. AC-7 covers the exact messages elsewhere, but the state-table row's own test no longer checks the message.
The PR claims 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the 'No match' state test was loosened in the final commit.
findings.fix: Restore the assertion, or disclose the change in the PR body.

findings.what: The 'Empty table' state test covers only the unfiltered view. The state table says the current filter can be any. AC-7 does cover the filtered views, so this is only a minor gap.
findings.fix: Also assert the nav's current filter when the table is empty and filtered.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent. The only addition is the traffic-config query allowance, which AC-8 requires and the PR discloses.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented and each is named by a test. The No match state test was weakened in the last commit.
Tests could not be run here, and CI runs them. A tautological assertion (toBeDefined) was introduced in the last commit.
The README describes the filter. Nothing stale found.
Filter values are validated against an allowlist and the query is parameterised. The empty-value case returns 400 as the spec requires. No defects found.
The title is HTML-escaped. The priority value is allowlisted before use, and the message uses only allowlisted values. No instructions planted in repo content.
src/index.js renders HTML, which is a user interface, but there are no styles or design assets to judge. The nav matches AC-5.
No browser was available. Rendered HTML is verified through the string assertions in the tests.
The claim that no tests were loosened is false: the last commit weakened the No match test. The title is under 72 characters.
